import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Filter for the latest available year to get a current snapshot
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
df_latest_year = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year].copy()

# Drop rows where dog gender information is missing, as it's crucial for this visualization
df_latest_year.dropna(subset=['SexHundLang'], inplace=True)

# Aggregate data: sum 'AnzHunde' (number of dogs) by age group and gender
# Use 'AlterVHundSort' to ensure correct chronological order of age groups on the plot
age_gender_counts = df_latest_year.groupby(['AlterVHundSort', 'AlterVHundLang', 'SexHundLang'])['AnzHunde'].sum().reset_index(name='Count')

# Pivot the table to prepare for a stacked bar chart
# 'AlterVHundLang' will be the index (x-axis), 'SexHundLang' will be columns (stacks), 'Count' will be values
age_gender_pivot = age_gender_counts.pivot(index='AlterVHundLang', columns='SexHundLang', values='Count').fillna(0)

# Ensure the age groups are sorted correctly on the x-axis
# Create a mapping from 'AlterVHundLang' to 'AlterVHundSort' from the filtered data
age_sort_map = df_latest_year[['AlterVHundLang', 'AlterVHundSort']].drop_duplicates().set_index('AlterVHundLang')['AlterVHundSort'].sort_values()
sorted_age_groups = age_sort_map.index.tolist()

# Reindex the pivot table with the sorted age groups
age_gender_pivot = age_gender_pivot.reindex(sorted_age_groups)

# Create the stacked bar chart
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))
age_gender_pivot.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, colormap='viridis', ax=plt.gca())

# Add titles and labels for clarity
plt.title(f'Dog Age Distribution by Gender in Zurich ({latest_year})', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Dog Age Group', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability if age groups are numerous
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=10)

# Add a legend for dog gender
plt.legend(title='Dog Gender', fontsize=10, title_fontsize=12)

# Add a grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
